title: Add cost-lattice chronograph and compact invocation snapshot service
author: Aisha Gomez
release_notes: Introduce a low-cardinality cost-lattice timeseries and a compact invocation snapshot service used by the chronograph dashboard for SLO triage. Adds safe rollout flags and sampling defaults; no customer-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: We've had repeated oncall churn diagnosing long-tail token cost/latency regressions where traces are expensive to store and slow to query. This PR adds two complementary pieces: 1) a 'cost-lattice chronograph' — an aggregated, multi-resolution timeseries that records cost and latency across prioritized token bands and request phases; 2) a compact invocation snapshot service that produces small (<=1KB) encoded summaries for sampled invocations to enable fast deck-level triage without full trace hydration.

What this does (high level):
- Cost-lattice chronograph: continuous rollups at 1s/10s/60s windows, broken out by token-phase (prefix, gen, streaming-chunk) and cost bucket (micro/normal/heavy). Stored in TSDB as low-cardinality series for rapid dashboarding and alert correlation.
- Invocation snapshot service: protobuf-lite encoder that picks a minimal set of fields (route, model, token_counts, kv_cache_hit_ratio, kernel_queue_ms, top-3 span durations) and compresses into a base64 blob. Snapshots are emitted to a sampled telemetry stream and indexed by snapshot_id in traces.
- Dashboard: new dashboard (dashboards/cost_lattice_chronograph.json) with heatmap + sparklines + snapshot quicklink for each anomaly.
- Alerts: tuning for token-burst alerts to use lattice aggregates and an adaptive suppression window to reduce false positives from transient spikes.
- Rollout: feature flag (observability.enable_chronograph) with server-side default off; default sample rate 0.5% global, 5% for customers in the internal beta cohort.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of chronograph rollup producer and storage schema.
- [x] Compact snapshot encoder + sampling hook.
- [x] Dashboard JSON and dashboard runbook section.
- [x] Unit + integration tests for encoder and rollup correctness.
- [x] CI passes and load test on staging for 24 hours.
- [x] Docs: observability/deskbook.md section added with triage guidance.

Safety notes: Snapshots are intentionally compact and do not include free-form user content. We validated that no prompt text or PII fields are included by construction; encoder explicitly drops raw prompt/body fields. Storage uses the existing telemetry retention policy for sampled artifacts (30 days by default).

Rollout plan: staged rollout in 3 phases over 3 weeks: internal beta -> opt-in customers -> global flag. We will monitor token-cost SLO and alert noise for the first 48h after each phase and have a rollback playbook (revert flag or lower sample rate).

Related: Linear ENG-2145 (lattice design), ENG-2190 (snapshot encoder). Jira SUP-4421 tracks support validation for customers in beta.

Summary of changed areas and intent: small, conservative instrumentation + a compact storage path to enable fast SRE/eng triage for cost/latency incidents. No changes to public APIs for inference clients.
